notes:
First-pass counts refer to the 71 draft sentences. 15 of 16 WebSearch calls used. Search summaries blend pages; claims were attributed to a URL only where that page's title or excerpt carried them (NHS migraine page and symptoms subpage, NHS inform, NICE CG150 recommendations/public page and QS42, Migraine Trust pages, MedlinePlus Managing migraines at home, NHS Scotland Right Decisions). Doubts: (1) 8-week diary minimum was missing from two NICE searches but returned by a third (NICE public page); kept. (2) candesartan/botulinum toxin attribution rests on blended NHS Scotland Right Decisions summaries. (3) brainstem-aura wording rests on the NINDS migraine page summary. (4) The ICHD-3 'typical aura' sentence rests on the NHS symptom list. Draft FAQ 'NICE ... diary' and 'Diagnosis relies on pattern' were removed or reworded. Added sentences a01-a06 are new or merged wording drawn from retrieved text, all supported.
CONTRADICTIONS or UNSUPPORTED in the EXISTING page entry (not edited): (a) treatment: 'Gepants are a newer class used alongside triptans' conflicts with the Migraine Trust, which describes gepants as an option when triptans cannot be taken or do not work. (b) prevention: 'limiting painkillers to fewer than 10 days a month' conflicts with sources: the Trust gives 15 or more days a month for over-the-counter painkillers (10 or more for triptans, opioids, combination painkillers); NICE 15 days or more for simple analgesics. (c) seekCare: 'headache that ... peaks within a minute' vs NICE QS42 wording 'within 5 minutes'; 'first-ever aura after 50', 'worst ever' and fever/stiff neck wording are not in the retrieved NHS 999 list (sudden extremely painful headache, speech or memory problems, vision loss, confusion, seizure, weakness on one side, recent head injury), and the page omits the NHS urgent (111/same-day GP) route. (d) overview: 'affects about one person in seven', 'leading cause of disability in young women', 'disorder of brain excitability rather than of blood vessels alone' (NHS says changes to nerves and blood vessels), cortical spreading depression, 'aura typically begins within the hour before the headache', and 'triggers precede an attack by less than two days' were not found in retrieved text. (e) riskFactors 'Age 20 to 50', complications 'slightly raised stroke risk ... smoking and the combined pill', signs 'normal examination', prevention 'losing weight if overweight' and 'Scans ... only for red-flag features' were not found. (f) treatment 'a triptan taken early' is not retrieved: NHS says take painkillers as soon as the headache starts. (g) 'aura ... a third of sufferers' and '4 to 72 hours' are supported (NHS 1 in 3; Trust/NHS 4 to 72 hours). (h) 'Chronic migraine (15 or more headache days a month)' is supported by the Trust.
